comment: The table of the rules of D17.13 for the pointers that C gives: an `extern fn` declaration names
the result, each parameter type of a function pointer parameter, and each pointer that a level
of a parameter holds where the parameter marks that level `mut`, through fixed arrays. Such a
type marks a level `mut` only where it says `own`, where a fixed parameter of the same type has
the mark, or where no parameter can carry a pointer; a function pointer type that C gives
follows the same rule. A `void*` result gives no type; a typed pointer result, `own` or not,
needs each parameter that can carry a pointer to point to its pointee with the marks aside, and
a function pointer result needs its type in each such parameter (the rule of the result type).
The rows cover first_given_mut, given_lacks_mut, result_lacks_type, gives_type_of,
has_param_of_type, marks_a_level_mut and report_given_mut of src/fort/check.ft, and the call in
resolve_fn. Each row breaks one part of the rules. The stages are the ffi fail corpus of
test/lang, whose tests pin each message, and check_extern_test.ft, which pins each position and
each declaration that the rules take. The table runs in the VM: pass a --runner that runs
tools/vm run in one slot and then syncs, as notes/environment.md says. The md5 guard reads the
product compiler that the build links. Put a row that an earlier run caught first, because the
first round of a run in the VM can read stale (notes/testing.md).
build: sleep 2 && touch src/fort/check.ft && ninja -C build/Linux/debug fort

stages.name: the extern suite
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std -j 4 check_extern_test

mutations.what: the result of an extern is no type that C gives
a parameter type of a function pointer parameter is no type that C gives
a pointer that a `mut` level of a parameter holds is no type that C gives
C stores a pointer at a level that the parameter does not mark `mut` too
the rule reads level 1 of a parameter alone
a fixed array that a level holds hides its pointers
the variable tail carries no pointer
a function pointer parameter carries no pointer
an extern with no parameter that can carry a pointer gives no storage of C
a type that says `own` is no new allocation
a parameter whose marks differ gives the `mut` too
a function pointer type that C gives follows no rule
a function pointer type that C gives has a variable tail
a type marks only its level 1
the error of a parameter stands at the result

mutations.old:
report_given_mut(ck, decl, s->name, g);
            sym_fail(ck, s);
mutations.what: a refused declaration keeps its symbol
an `own` at level 2 exempts the type too
only the first parameter can carry a pointer
a later parameter of a callback clears the type that an earlier one gave
a typed pointer result needs no parameter of its pointee
the rule of the result type reports before the rule of the `mut` of the result
a function pointer type that C gives reports its result type as a `mut`
the rule of the result type gives the text of the rule of the `mut`
the error of the result type stands at the first parameter
a `void*` result needs each parameter to point to its pointee
a function pointer result is no pointer result
a typed result that says `own` needs no parameter of its pointee
the variable tail carries no pointer of another type
a function pointer parameter carries no pointer of another type
each data pointer, a `void*` included, points to the pointee of the result
the pointees compare with each mark
each function pointer parameter has the type of a function pointer result
